question: In the tagged template proposal issue, what is the max pool size in the POC?

done.answer:
brianc/node-postgres #3745: Add a sql tagged template function

State: closed

postgres.js has a nice API for queries:
```js
const users = await sql`SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = ${id}`
```

Values become parameters, never string concatenation, and the driver prepares and reuses the statement automatically.

I think pg can offer the same with the machinery it already has. A tagged template receives the same frozen strings array on every call from the same call site, so a `WeakMap` on it gives a stable statement name with no hashing. The tag only has to build `{ name, text, values }` and pass it to `query()`: named statements already skip re-parsing per connection, and with #3739 the queries also pipeline through `pool.query()`, postgres.js style.

Open points:
- an option to skip the statement name, for pgbouncer in transaction mode?
- recovery when a schema change invalidates a prepared statement (postgres.js retries once)?
- composition (nested fragments, identifiers) can come later, values only is already useful?

I would like to work on this. Is a PR welcome, and would you prefer it in core or as a separate package?

POC

```js
const { sql } = new Pool({ max: 2, pipeline: true });

const id = 7;
const users = await sql`SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = ${id}`;
```

WIP https://github.com/brianc/node-postgres/compare/master...nigrosimone:node-postgres:sql-template-tag [Source 1]

for this we  use https://github.com/felixfbecker/node-sql-template-strings which does exactly this, and has been battle-tested (we use it for our several millions query day production app)

Indeed, It could be included in node-postgres for to ease usage for all new users who perhaps don't know this library

> Values become parameters, never string concatenation, and the driver prepares and reuses the statement automatically.

with node-sql-template-strings, you still have to provide a name (with `setName`) to have a prepared statement, which is well (we don't always want to use a prepared statement because of the cost for very simple queries)

## Comment 2
Source: https://github.com/brianc/node-postgres/issues/3745#issuecomment-5265729687

@abenhamdine 
It would be convenient to have this function in pg because you can get the connection directly from the pool
```js
await SQL`SELECT author FROM books WHERE name = ${book} AND author = ${author}`
```
instead of
```js
await pg.query(SQL`SELECT author FROM books WHERE name = ${book} AND author = ${author}`)
```
or find a "trick" to do it in node-sql-template-strings, eg:

```js
import { magicTrick } from "node-sql-template-strings";

const pool = new Pool();

await SQL`SELECT author FROM books WHERE name = ${book} AND author = ${author}`
```

side note: https://github.com/felixfbecker/node-sql-template-strings is active? last commit is 7 years ago, just to understand if it's worth doing a PR

brianc/node-postgres #3745: Add a sql tagged template function

State: closed

postgres.js has a nice API for queries:
```js
const users = await sql`SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = ${id}`
```

Values become parameters, never string concatenation, and the driver prepares and reuses the statement automatically.

I think pg can offer the same with the machinery it already has. A tagged template receives the same frozen strings array on every call from the same call site, so a `WeakMap` on it gives a stable statement name with no hashing. The tag only has to build `{ name, text, values }` and pass it to `query()`: named statements already skip re-parsing per connection, and with #3739 the queries also pipeline through `pool.query()`, postgres.js style.

Open points:
- an option to skip the statement name, for pgbouncer in transaction mode?
- recovery when a schema change invalidates a prepared statement (postgres.js retries once)?
- composition (nested fragments, identifiers) can come later, values only is already useful?

I would like to work on this. Is a PR welcome, and would you prefer it in core or as a separate package?

POC

```js
const { sql } = new Pool({ max: 2, pipeline: true });

const id = 7;
const users = await sql`SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = ${id}`;
```

# brianc/node-postgres #3745: Add a sql tagged template function

State: closed

postgres.js has a nice API for queries:
```js
const users = await sql`SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = ${id}`
```

Values become parameters, never string concatenation, and the driver prepares and reuses the statement automatically.

I think pg can offer the same with the machinery it already has. A tagged template receives the same frozen strings array on every call from the same call site, so a `WeakMap` on it gives a stable statement name with no hashing. The tag only has to build `{ name, text, values }` and pass it to `query()`: named statements already skip re-parsing per connection, and with #3739 the queries also pipeline through `pool.query()`, postgres.js style.

Open points:
- an option to skip the statement name, for pgbouncer in transaction mode?
- recovery when a schema change invalidates a prepared statement (postgres.js retries once)?
- composition (nested fragments, identifiers) can come later, values only is already useful?

I would like to work on this. Is a PR welcome, and would you prefer it in core or as a separate package?

POC

```js
const { sql } = new Pool({ max: 2, pipeline: true });

const id = 7;
const users = await sql`SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = ${id}`;
```

## Comment 6
Source: https://github.com/brianc/node-postgres/issues/3745#issuecomment-5372294640

The idea above is now a working package: https://github.com/nigrosimone/pg-telaio (`npm i pg-telaio`).

It is the tag described here, built on top of the Pool the application already has: values become $n parameters, `prepare: true` names the statements automatically and retries once when a schema change (0A000) or a transaction-mode pgbouncer (26000) kills one, and unawaited fragments compose. Underneath it keeps a few connections in pipeline mode for as long as pool.query() cannot pipeline (#3739), with a guard so a slow query does not hold the fast ones queued behind it. On a primary key read with 3 connections and 64 queries in flight it does about 3.4x pool.query().

If you want this in core, I am happy to integrate all of it there and retire the library. Otherwise it stays a separate package on pg's public API.
